title: Should I be generating my assets with AI?
author: Wooden_chest
selftext:
I'm a game developer that currently doesn't use any AI for assets, though I do use AI for code.

I am capable lf creating assets myself, whether that be models, textures, fonts, sounds, music or anything else, and I do enjoy the process and it is fun.

However, I'm seeing AI generated assets' quality be on par with handmade assets, so I'm wondering if I'm just wasting my time and should be generating them instead. I'm afraid I've chosen the wrong path and am doing a disservice to myself by not using AI for assets.

I'm not on any sort of deadlines as I'm solo and doing it for fun, but I would like to complete my work in reasonable time.

I came to this community as it has people experienced with this question.

Thanks.

Try to generate one asset, then ask ai to generate a similar asset, then compare. If it’s acceptable to you or not.

You generate an image of a vampire. Looks good, except he has a gold chain that blends into his skin. The art is 90% perfect with a big flaw. Redraw that part.

You generate a 3D model of a car. It looks perfect but the wheels are not perfectly round, because they're rendered as a polygon with lots of sides, not spherical. Replace the wheel with a cylinder.

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body:
This question is asked here on a weekly or biweekly basis. Essentially the second it falls off the front page it crops up again.

This isn't a question of IF you should be generating assets with AI. It's a question of if you're able to maintain consistent quality with your assets whether you use handmade or  AI generated, or a hybrid. Quality, consistency and polish are what matter here. Most people who rely on generative assets don't know enough about art to maintain consistency or polish, so even if the base generated asset is of high individual quality, the game falls apart because nothing matches or because there are inherent problems (like animation frames not actually making sense or lighting clashing, or the UI, backgrounds and character sprites all being at odds with one another, or even worse having individual character sprites not matching the same style as others.)

Most people in this sub are not hypocritical to think that AI use is fine for some things (like coding) and not fine for other things (like drawing). Many of us were/are  programmers or in a related field. I, at least, find it fucking stupid that some people seem to think it's OK for AI to have stolen our work (and they happily use it to help them edit their videos or update their web portfolios or ask GPT to write them shit) but not OK to touch on THEIR livelihood (I was both programmer and graphic designer, so I had a foot on both sides of the fence, but from what I've seen traditional artists don't care if you were drawing UIs / logos with your pen or designing complex javascript animations, they only consider your work sacred if you were drawing anime waifus on deviant art.

comments.body: Tbh generating a proper ready to use asset takes as much time if not more than drawing them yourself. It usually smells like AI and has leftover inconsistencies. Keeping the same painting style in hundreds/thousands of assets is near impossible. I'd draw everything by hand if I could.

comments.body: The easier way to fasten your workflow is to ask AI to create concept art, and then recreate/rework it to make it consistent. It's maybe not the way to create final assets (today) but truly increase the amount of work you can finish in the smaller time.

comments.body: i generate all my assets using ai. 2d character animation is very tough. I figured out hard way.  but i learnt recently that if you create 3d model and rig it then creating animation using it is simpler relatively. So i am switching to 3d model lately.

comments.author: _ghost_jihan_
comments.body: Make things yourself when you enjoy it, and use AI for quick concepts, placeholders, or repetitive work. If the process is part of the fun, speed isn’t everything.
